summary: This is a humorous RFC. It imagines an "Internet Protocol Police" charged with punishing willful violations of the "Collected Wisdom of the IETF community", and it sets out a schedule of punishments for such infractions. It is Informational and is not a real protocol specification.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9948 is an April 1st joke about an imaginary Internet Protocol Police. It lists pretend punishments and explains what common protocol-review comments might mean.

subtitle: An April 1st schedule of punishments from the imaginary Internet Protocol Police.

tldr.problem: This April 1st joke imagines an Internet Protocol Police responsible for punishing violations of the IETF community's collected wisdom.
tldr.mechanism: It lists five imaginary punishments and translates common reviewer comments into blunt, humorous meanings.
tldr.outcome: The RFC satirizes protocol review and community norms. It describes no real police force or actual punishment process.

today: RFC 9948 is an Informational document published on April 1, 2026. Its Internet Protocol Police and punishment schedule are fictional satire about IETF review.

sections.title: The Imaginary Protocol Police
sections.content: RFC 9948 imagines that the Internet Protocol Police (IPP) punish willful violations of the IETF community's collected wisdom. It says the schedule had been applied informally and presents its publication as a way to enlighten the community. The document is humorous.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC invents a police force for protocol design. The force and its rules are part of the April 1st joke.

sections.title: The Schedule of Punishments
sections.content: The schedule names the Raised Eyebrow, the Frown, the Shaking of the Head, the Finger Wag, and the Head-in-Hand Gesture. The RFC assigns these to examples such as inconsistent terminology, unregistered code points, hidden complexity, and infractions described in RFC 4041. The last punishment is described as mythical.
sections.plainLanguage: The five penalties range from an eyebrow raise to a mythical head-in-hand gesture. Each is attached to a different kind of alleged design mistake.

sections.title: What Reviewers May Be Saying
sections.content: The RFC lists common reviewer phrases and gives satirical interpretations. For example, “This may work in the lab, but ...” is said to signal missing or naive operational considerations. The text says these verbal comments are guidance, not punishments, and rejects wet noodles as a suitable measure.
sections.plainLanguage: The document humorously decodes familiar review comments. It explicitly says that these comments are guidance, not formal penalties.
